source.citation: Lawrence C. Earle, "Dearborn Street Bridge", colour reproduction of a bank mural, in Chicago, Historical, Pictorial (Chicago National Bank; Chicago: Rand, McNally & Co., catalogued c1902), plate facing printed p.18. Exact Internet Archive scan n24; explanatory text p.18 at n23; artist attribution p.6 at n10; title n6 and Chicago printer imprint n5.
what_it_does_not_supply: An exact1July1835 scene or surveyed picture location
A measured footprint, deck width, draw rise or timber scantling
The same physical projection as the Andreas engraving or an independent contemporary witness
A licence for a modern separately supplied museum/stock reproduction
Any rights clearance for the separate Baker-Co Old Point engraving
what_it_supplies: The image is a retrospective depiction of the first Dearborn Street drawbridge, built1834 and removed1839, rather than the1849 swing bridge
Two gallows frames and high shore braces over a rising closed draw profile
Boarded bridge parapets and timber approach/support masses as pictured
A warm-brown painted representation, without proving the historical timber finish
Original book credits Earle and describes retrospective research for the Chicago National Bank mural series
